title: Texture avenues for the world
question: Which avenues should we try?

media.caption: The reference for polish and vibe

options.label: 1. Hand-painted tiling textures
options.note: Painted tile, plaster, carpet, wood and metal textures on every surface, mapped by world position so no prop needs UVs. 2-3 days, moderate frame cost.

options.label: 2. Procedural materials in the shader
options.note: The same kinds of surfaces computed in the shader: tile-by-tile variation, chips, carpet fibre, plaster clouding, brushed metal. 3-4 days, no textures.

options.label: 3. Decals and wear
options.note: A lived-in layer: scuffs, worn carpet paths, coffee rings, tape marks, stains and stickers from one painted atlas. 1-2 days, cheap.

options.label: 4. Vertex colour and baked light
options.note: No pattern, but no flat faces: darker corners, warmer faces toward windows, gentle floor gradients, varied tints on repeated props. 1 day, free at runtime.

options.label: 5. Painted surfaces from our own art
options.note: Repaint each room from its play camera with our anime model and project the painting back onto floors and walls. Closest to our generated images; 4-6 days plus approval per room.

options.label: 6. Gloss, reflections and sheen
options.note: Floors that catch window and lamp reflections, metal highlights, fabric sheen; materials read as different without textures. 1-2 days; the floor reflection would be desktop only.

options.label: 7. Trim sheets
options.note: One painted atlas of edge and panel detail (vents, screws, skirting, label strips) mapped onto props. 3-5 days, touches every prop builder.

options.label: 8. Small modelled detail
options.note: Bevels, frames, cables, paper piles and handles modelled in. About a day per room; adds detail more than texture.

links.label: Full write-up: what you'd see, references, how it's built, costs and risks

decision: Picked 2, 3, 4, 7 and 8: try them in a small showcase room so we can see the different effects (now style-avenues-room)
